summary: Weekly POC sync to review INT8 vs FP8 quantization runs. INT8 shows 2.8-3.5x throughput improvements and 40-55% cost reduction on tokens/sec in our infra, but certain prompt classes show quality regressions (short instruction following + code examples). FP8 retains quality but with smaller perf gains. Action: run targeted diffs, tune per-layer quantization scales, and try mixed-precision fallback for sensitive routes.
topics: deployment strategy: staged rollouts, mixed precision, fallback
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-08
Time: 10:00 PT
Duration: 45 min
Attendees: Alyssa Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Redwood CSM), Daniel Kim (AtlasDocs ML Eng), Rita Gomez (AtlasDocs Infra), Tom Walker (AtlasDocs CTO)
Shared artifacts: results spreadsheet https://redwood.app/drive/atlasdocs-quant-results, demo recordings, security FAQ link (Alyssa to send)

[00:00] Alyssa: okay everyone good morning thanks for joining, want to keep this to 45, quick recap from last week, Marco ran the int8 pass across your baseline and we got some perf numbers back.
[00:17] Marco: yeah hi all, sorry slight echo, but yeah i ran the INT8 run on the staging model replicas you gave us, same prompts as last week, details in the spreadsheet link i pasted. overall throughput up ~3x at 8 token batching, p95 latency down ~35% on average.
[00:45] Daniel: nice, that's promising — can you remind us what HW you used? we are on A100s in prod but staging was V100-ish.
[01:05] Marco: staging was A100-sxm2 40GB, single-socket, using Redwood runtime with per-layer calibration and symmetric INT8. we also tried FP8 (E4-style) on a subset — FP8 kept much of the fp16 quality but only gave ~1.4x throughput.
[01:30] Rita: so INT8 gives best perf but more regressions? what's the magnitude on accuracy or hallucination?
[01:45] Marco: good question. aggregate metrics: exact-match-ish metrics dropped 0.8-2.5% across general QA benchmarks; however on your internal short-instruction set (the ticket-summary prompts) we saw bigger drops — up to 6% drop in relevance/precision. some code generation snippets lost token-level formatting — weird tokenization shifts.
[02:15] Daniel: that's the concern. our main traffic is short instruction->structured output; even small regressions are risky.
[02:30] Alyssa: totally understand. what we recommend is a mixed strategy: use INT8 for bulk routes (search summarization, embeddings, large-context generation) and keep FP16/FP8 for critical short-instruction routes. we can also do per-route model variants and automatic fallback in Redwood so callers don't see downtime.
[03:00] Tom: is that per-request routing handled in the control plane or at inference runtime? how much engineering work on our side?
[03:15] Marco: it's control-plane config + request header routing; minimal code changes. you tag the route, we set policy to route to INT8 variant with automatic detection of quality regressions to fallback. if you prefer we can run A/B with canary and % rollout.
[03:40] Priya: note for the pilot we should enable tracing so we can correlate token-level diffs to user sessions. Marco we'll enable that?
[03:50] Marco: yes we'll add per-token diffs and sample traces to the shared sheet.
[04:05] Daniel: can you describe how calibration works? last time calibration was causing variance between runs.
[04:20] Marco: sure. we do a two-pass calibration: collect activation statistics on representative prompts (your sample set), compute scale factors per-channel, then quantize weights/activations. the tricky bit is outlier layers where a few heads have large activation spikes; for those we either keep FP16 or use layerwise clipped scaling. that's where FP8 helps a bit — it's more forgiving on dynamic range.
[04:55] Rita: how reproducible are the runs? we saw run-to-run noise earlier.
[05:05] Marco: there's some noise due to micro-batching scheduling and CUDA kernel paths; after warmup runs variance drops to <1.5% on throughput. quality diffs are deterministic given the same calibration snapshot though.
[05:30] Daniel: what about memory footprint? INT8 should reduce KV cache size?
[05:40] Marco: yes approx 2x reduction in KV memory footprint which lets you push longer contexts or larger batch sizes. FP8 gives some reduction (~1.3x) but not as much.
[05:55] Tom: any compatibility issues with your dedicated infra? in Dedicated we'll want reserved capacity.
[06:05] Alyssa: Dedicated supports INT8/FP8 runtime; the runtime will pick kernels accordingly. if you want a private deployment we can provide same control plane but with on-prem options; KMS integration is available for keys.
[06:25] Daniel: on quality: can we get per-prompt diffs? want to understand which prompts break.
[06:35] Marco: yes i extracted top 50 regressions and uploaded to the sheet with before/after tokens and a delta column; link is in chat. for example prompt ID 347 shows a missing table element on INT8, FP8 kept it.
[07:00] Rita: are these mostly early-layer quantization issues or final-layer logits?
[07:10] Marco: mixed; we saw both. some are early-layer numerical noise that propagates, others are final logit shifts for rare tokens. we're instrumenting per-layer activation histograms which should identify hot layers.
[07:35] Daniel: ok sounds like we need a triage: (1) produce per-prompt diffs, (2) flag high-risk routes, (3) try mixed-precision for flagged routes.
[07:50] Alyssa: agreed. action items: Marco will run targeted evals (we'll add to sheet). Daniel to deploy INT8 to staging branch for 2 weeks. Alyssa to send pricing update + contract.
[08:05] Tom: question on rollback — if we detect a regression in-prod, how fast can we fallback?
[08:15] Marco: immediate at the control plane level, requests routed to FP16 variant; since models are staged we can switch traffic with config change in under 30s. caching/prefix issues can cause some in-flight variance but generally quick.
[08:35] Daniel: cost numbers — can you give ballpark per-token savings?
[08:45] Marco: based on our runs: INT8 reduces per-token compute cost ~40-55% depending on batch. FP8 is ~20-30%. net on your observed traffic mix you could see up to ~45% cost reduction if majority routes move to INT8.
[09:05] Rita: network overhead for model variants? extra replicas?
[09:15] Marco: you may need more model variants pinned, but overall memory savings with INT8 reduces replica sizes so net infra often lowers. We'll provide a recommended capacity plan in the sheet.
[09:35] Daniel: any difference in tokenization/hashing that causes the formatting loss?
[09:45] Marco: not tokenization specifically; it's numerical differences leading to early termination of a sequence or different high-prob tokens. we'll instrument logits distribution to catch that.
[10:05] Alyssa: can we also talk briefly about security? Tom/Rita have questions about SOC2 and VPC.
[10:15] Tom: yes we need updated security docs and proof-of-SOC2 for Dedicated pilots.
[10:25] Alyssa: i'll send the SOC2 attestation and security FAQ. Dedicated supports VPC peering and KMS; we can set up a private control plane if needed.
[10:40] Priya: note for the pilot success criteria: 1) quality regression <2% on critical short-instruction routes, 2) cost reduction >30% net, 3) no functional regressions on top 200 prompts. we'll formalize this.
[10:55] Daniel: sounds good. Marco, do you have a hypothesis on how to reduce the short-instruction regression?
[11:05] Marco: yes — a few paths: refine calibration dataset to include more short-instruction examples; keep final decoder blocks in FP16 (partial quantization); increase per-channel clipping on problematic heads; or use FP8 for those sensitive layers. We'll test 3 variants and report.
[11:35] Tom: timeline?
[11:40] Marco: we'll run the experiments week of 12/14 and aim to share results by 12/15.
[11:50] Alyssa: great. last thing — i'll update the pilot contract and pricing and put the next check-in on 2026-12-22. does that work?
[12:02] Daniel: yes that's fine. thanks everyone.

Recap / Next steps:
- Marco to run per-prompt diffs + per-layer histograms and upload detailed sheet by 2026-12-15.
- Daniel to deploy INT8 variant in staging for 2 weeks and collect traces by 2026-12-22.
- Alyssa to send pricing, SOC2, and pilot contract draft by 2026-12-09.

End of transcript.
